$about: THE CORRECTING-LINE LEDGER, BASE UI ARM. Same job and same rules as
`ledger.react-aria.json`: every `text` below must still occur in its component's files
exactly `occurrences` times as a CODE line, or `measure.mjs` aborts.
── ONE DEFINITION IS HELD FIXED ACROSS THE TWO ARMS, ON PURPOSE ────────────────
A `correcting` line is one that exists to fix an upstream DEFECT: a leaked English
string, an unnamed control, a dangling idref, a direction bug, or behaviour upstream
drops. It is NOT every line the engine swap cost.
The Base UI port also carries a large body of pure API-TRANSLATION code — the
destructured React Aria prop names, the `attr()` spreads that rename them, the
`_unused` discards for props with no Base UI equivalent. Those lines are real and they
are expensive, and they are DELIBERATELY NOT IN THIS FILE, because folding them into
`correcting` would silently redefine the axis between the two arms and make
`totals.correcting_lines` a comparison of two different quantities. They fall into the
harness's mechanical `structure` bucket, where the line-count growth is still visible,
and they are counted separately and reported in
`experiments/measurements/comparison.json` under `api_translation_census`.
`base-ui-adapter.ts` is likewise absent: the harness reads exactly a component's
`file` and `variantsFile`, and the adapter is a THIRD shared module the React Aria
arm did not have. Its cost is measured whole and reported in comparison.json under
`shared_module_cost`, which is the honest place for a module four components import.
── WHAT SURVIVED, WHAT DIED, WHAT IS NEW ──────────────────────────────────────
SURVIVED, unchanged in text: every `required-prop-shim` on an announced string.
IconButton.label, IconToggle.label, CheckboxGroup.label, TabList.label,
Slider.label, NumberField's four, ComboBox's two, Dialog.closeLabel,
Select.placeholder. Neither library requires any of them, so neither library can
take them away — which is the clearest single result in this arm.
DIED, and each is a genuine subtraction:
slider `insetInlineStart: 0,` / `inlineSize: ...`  Base UI's Slider.Indicator sets
both itself.
slider `aria-label={label}` (the second one)       the useSlot dangling-IDREF
branch has no Base UI equivalent,
so the thumb needs one label, not
two.
slider `<I18nProvider locale={...}>`               replaced, NOT removed — see
`DirectionProvider` below, which
is the same defect with a new
cause.
number-field `slot="increment"` / `slot="decrement"`  Base UI ships dedicated
Increment/Decrement parts.
number-field `decrementAriaLabel=` / `incrementAriaLabel=`  the belt-and-braces
second application is gone; Base
UI builds no competing
aria-labelledby.
combobox/select/menu `resolvedTextValue` on ComboBoxItem  Combobox.Item has no
per-item label hook at all, so the
line could not be kept even to
serve SSR.
NEW, and every one of them is a Base-UI-shaped hole:
select      a Lumo React context, because Base UI publishes no placeholder or
aria-label down the tree the way RAC's SelectContext did.
combobox    a `useId` and a NATIVE `<label htmlFor>`, because `Combobox.Label`
labels the TRIGGER and leaves the `<input role="combobox">` with a
computed name of `null`.
menu        two contexts — one to reproduce RAC's per-level placement defaults, one
to dispatch `onAction`, which Base UI's items do not have — plus a
hand-written `role="none"` on the box between menu and menuitems.
slider      a `DirectionProvider`, because direction is no longer derived from the
locale, and `getAriaValueText`, because Base UI's default is `undefined`
for a single-thumb slider.
popover/tooltip/dialog  a positional child split and a `render={}` lift, because
Base UI has no ButtonContext and its trigger must be a literal element.
`kind` vocabulary is `ledger.react-aria.json`'s, unchanged, so the two
`correcting_by_kind` maps compare directly.

corrections.why: Subtracts the optional `aria-label` so the only way to name an icon-only button is the required `label`. Base UI does not require a name either — the line is unchanged from the React Aria arm because the rule is Lumo's, not the engine's.
An icon is not a name. A prototype shipped 33 unnamed controls under the convention this replaces.

corrections.text: export function IconButton({ label, size = "md", className, ...props }: IconButtonProps) {
corrections.why: The whole component exists to make the name a constructor argument.
Applies the required name to the control Base UI would otherwise leave unnamed.
Unchanged. Removes the inherited `isInvalid` so it can be re-declared with an explicit `| undefined` under exactOptionalPropertyTypes.
A group announced as bare "group" is the named-controls defect. Base UI's CheckboxGroup emits role=group + aria-labelledby and requires no label, exactly as RAC did.
The re-declaration the Omit above makes room for.

An explicit `undefined` is a type error against Base UI's `invalid?: boolean`, so the prop must be conditionally spread rather than passed. Same defect as the React Aria arm's `optional("isInvalid", …)`, one prop name later.

Renders the required group name. `nativeLabel={false}` is the Base-UI-specific half: there is no single control for a `<label for>` to point at, and a native label here would claim to focus a control that does not exist. The name reaches the group through aria-labelledby instead.
The name itself.
Same subtraction as IconButton. A nameless toggle announces "button, pressed" — information-shaped and empty.
Required name for an icon-only toggle.

corrections.why: The split component that carries the requirement.
Applies it.

Once on SelectProps and once on the Lumo context that carries it down. Still required, for an INVERTED reason: RAC rendered its own English `selectPlaceholder`; Base UI's `<Select.Value>` renders EMPTY, which is worse because there is no Latin word for a gate or a reviewer to catch.

RAC delivered the root's `placeholder` and `aria-label` to descendants through its own context. Base UI publishes neither, and expects aria-label on Select.Trigger rather than on the root, so the wrapper has to carry them itself.
The provider half.
The consumer half, in SelectTrigger and SelectValue.
Puts the root's announced name on the element Base UI actually reads it from.
Applies the required placeholder to Select.Value, which is where Base UI wants it and where RAC did not need it.

corrections.text: const resolvedTextValue = textValue ?? (typeof children === "string" ? children : undefined);
corrections.why: Kept for a DIFFERENT reason than in the React Aria arm. RAC derived typeahead text only from a literal string child and the check-mark wrapper destroyed it; Base UI's `Select.Item.label` defaults to the item's DOM text content and cannot be broken by a wrapper — but there is no DOM during a server render, which is the tier this library is measured at.
Conditional spread, and the prop name is now Base UI's `label`.

Doing LESS work than in the React Aria arm: Base UI's own `side` union carries 'inline-start'/'inline-end' as first-class values, so the logical spelling is a real union member rather than one of two equally-valid options. The narrowing stays because the public API may not change.

RAC published 'bottom start' for a root menu and 'end top' for a submenu through PopoverContext, so a MenuPopover that set nothing got both right. Base UI's Positioner defaults to side=bottom align=center at EVERY level and publishes nothing per level, so a submenu opens BELOW its parent item. This flag is how the two defaults are reproduced without asking the caller.

corrections.text: const { side, align } = placementToSideAlign(placement ?? (nested ? "end top" : "bottom start"));
corrections.why: The defaults themselves, restated in the wrapper because the engine no longer supplies them.
Resets the level at the popup, so a menu nested two deep takes its placement from its own SubmenuTrigger rather than inheriting its grandparent's.

corrections.text: const MenuActionContext = createContext<((key: string) => void) | null>(null);
corrections.why: RAC's collection had one action callback on the list and dispatched it with the activated key. Base UI has no collection and no `onAction`; its items take a plain onClick, so the dispatch is composed here.
The dispatch itself.

RAC's <Menu> WAS the role=menu element; Base UI puts that role on Menu.Popup, one level up, leaving this box as an unroled generic between a menu and its menuitems. `role="none"` is what keeps the tree conforming, and its absence would read fine in review.

corrections.text: const resolvedTextValue = textValue ?? (typeof children === "string" ? children : undefined);
corrections.why: Server-side typeahead text. See select.

Conditional spread — an object-literal property here rather than a JSX spread, because MenuItem builds one `shared` props object it hands to three different Base UI parts (Item, LinkItem, SubmenuTrigger).
Unchanged, and the glyph was never the engine's: the submenu arrow is a real element carrying U+203A rather than an SVG chevron, because U+203A is Bidi_Mirrored and an SVG path is not.
The mirrored glyph itself.
Closing the same element.

Still required, and the reason inverts. RAC wrote aria-label="Show suggestions" unconditionally; Base UI's Combobox.Trigger renders an icon-only <button> with NO name at all, which is the more common of the two defects and leaves no Latin word behind.
As above, for the list. RAC's was "Suggestions"; Base UI's is nothing.
Destructured off the root because the leaking element is buried inside.
Likewise.
Applied directly to Combobox.Trigger. No context to lose to any more.
Applied to Combobox.List.

NEW. `<Combobox.Label>` labels the TRIGGER, not the input — Base UI says so in a dev warning. Measured with it in place: the <input role="combobox"> carried no aria-labelledby, no aria-label, and computed a name of `null`. The id is chosen here rather than left to Base UI so a native `<label htmlFor>` can pair with it IN THE FIRST BYTE; useId is SSR-stable, a layout effect is not.
The chosen id, handed to the Root so Base UI stamps it on the input rather than generating its own.
A NATIVE label, not Base UI's, because Base UI's would name the wrong element. RAC wired the same composition through LabelContext with nothing asked of the caller.
exactOptionalPropertyTypes against Base UI's `placeholder?: string`.
Unchanged. Moves IconButton's requirement one level up so a dialog written by someone who never read button.tsx still cannot ship an unnamed ✕.
Destructured. The React Aria arm carried the whole signature on one line; the Base UI arm's parameter list is long enough to wrap, so this is the line that survives.

The Base UI form of the React Aria arm's `slot="close"`. RAC published a ButtonContext whose `close` slot supplied onPress; Base UI has no slots, so closing is `Dialog.Close render={…}` merging an onClick onto the element it is given. Same claim, different mechanism — and the mechanism is why this is a measured gap: IconButton is an RAC Button that drives from onPress.
Applies the required name.

The Base UI form of `slot="title"`. Without it the dialog is labelled by its TRIGGER's text instead of its heading — a different sentence, and no error. Base UI's Title writes its own id into the Root's store; the cost is that it THROWS outside a Dialog.Root, where RAC's Heading degraded to a plain <h2>.
Unchanged, and still load-bearing: seven still-React-Aria components consume this type.
Derived from RAC's own union rather than retyped, so a RAC release that adds a value stays in sync.
The subtraction itself. Doing less work than it did: Base UI's `side` union already treats the logical spellings as first-class.
Removes RAC's wider placement so the narrowed one can replace it.
The replacement.

NEW, and the same shape recurs in dialog.tsx and tooltip.tsx. RAC's DialogTrigger wired its first child IMPLICITLY, publishing a ButtonContext carrying onPress, aria-expanded and aria-haspopup that any RAC Button descendant picked up. Base UI has no such context: its trigger must be a literal element or a `render={}` lift, so the wrapper splits children positionally to keep the public API.
The split.
The split.
The split.
The lift. What it cannot recover is that the child is an RAC Button driving from onPress while Base UI merges an onClick.

Imported rather than restated, and now importing the translation TABLE as well as the type: two hand-filtered copies of the same union drift the first time RAC adds a value, and two copies of the placement mapping drift the first time Base UI does.
Removes the physical spellings.

The split.

Subtracts the optional aria-label so `label` is the only way in.
Neither library emits English here — the tablist simply arrives unnamed, announced as bare "tab list". Identical defect, identical fix, both engines.

REPLACES the React Aria arm's second `I18nProvider`, and the defect it fixes is worse. RAC's useSlider resolved thumb positions from useLocale().direction, so one provider fixed geometry as a side effect. Base UI has no locale context at all: `locale` and direction are two independent props with two independent failure modes.

corrections.text: import { FORMAT_LOCALE, cn, direction, formatNumber, type Locale } from "@lumo-ui/core";
corrections.why: `formatNumber` because Slider.Value's default children are the runtime-locale string; `direction` because it is the only thing that can connect the required `locale` to Base UI's direction context; `FORMAT_LOCALE` because Base UI's `locale` prop wants the extension tag.
Subtracts the optional aria-label and the formatOptions that would otherwise reach only one of the two value renderings.
An unnamed role=group wrapping an unnamed range input announces as bare "slider". Base UI emits no English here either.
REQUIRED, and now the single input to THREE things rather than two: the visible output, aria-valuetext, and the reading direction.
Re-declared so the same options reach Intl.NumberFormat and Base UI's own formatter, which is what keeps the two renderings from drifting.
Destructured.

The provider. Without it a Persian page renders Persian digits sliding the wrong way, with nothing red anywhere — the same measured failure as the React Aria arm's missing I18nProvider (left:40% where left:60% belongs), reached by a different route.
Closing it.
Base UI's per-component locale prop. There is no provider to set it once.

ONCE, where the React Aria arm needed it twice. RAC's SliderThumb useSlot started true and emitted an aria-labelledby pointing at a <Label> the component never rendered; Base UI has no such branch, so the second application — a pure dangling-IDREF fix — is gone. This one is here because the hidden <input type=range> is what a screen reader lands on.

Base UI's getDefaultAriaValueText returns UNDEFINED for a single-thumb slider with no format, so a slider left alone emits NO aria-valuetext at all and a screen reader falls back to aria-valuenow in the user agent's digits. Quieter than RAC's Latin `40`: no string to grep for, no attribute to diff.
The value the callback returns — the same call as the visible output, so the two cannot drift.

Slider.Value's own children would be the string Base UI formatted under its own `locale` handling; routing both numbers through one @lumo-ui/core call is what makes them identical rather than merely similar.
Conditional spread, and the prop rename — RAC's formatOptions is Base UI's format.
